label: Dr. Robert M. Wood
narrative: Robert M. Wood is the aerospace-industry end of the retrieval literature. He holds a doctorate in physics and spent forty-three years at McDonnell Douglas, where he managed advanced propulsion and effects research - including, on his own account, a company-funded study in the late 1960s and early 1970s into whether UFO field-propulsion effects could be replicated. That places him in the same institutional category as Stanton Friedman: a cleared contractor engineer who concluded from the inside that a compartmented programme was plausible. With his son Ryan S. Wood he built The Majestic Documents project, an online archive at majesticdocuments.com which since 1999 has collected, published, catalogued and applied a stated authenticity-rating scheme to the MJ-12 and related leaked-document corpus - including the Special Operations Manual SOM1-01, the 'Interplanetary Phenomenon Unit' material, and the Air Accident Report papers. The project's importance to this board is methodological rather than evidentiary: Wood insisted on treating the documents as forensic objects - typeface, paper, watermark, ink, format, security-marking convention and internal administrative plausibility - rather than as scripture, and published the ratings. Whether one accepts the conclusions, the framework is the only sustained forensic protocol ever applied to the leaked-document corpus, and no agency has ever published a competing analysis.
